question: Per kilogram, which burns the most energy at rest: the heart, the brain, the liver, muscle or fat?
answer: The heart, then the brain. By Elia's measurements a kilogram of heart burns about 440 kcal a day and of brain about 240, against 13 for resting muscle. The brain, 2% of body weight, takes about a fifth of resting energy, most of it pumping back the ions that cross neurons' membranes at every signal.
move: When something is said to burn a lot, ask: per what, and when?
reference: Elia, M. (1992) Organ and tissue contribution to metabolic rate, in Kinney & Tucker (eds), Energy Metabolism: Tissue Determinants and Cellular Corollaries, Raven Press, 61-79; Wang et al. (2010) American Journal of Clinical Nutrition 92: 1369-1377

items.label: Muscle
items.note: Add 2 kg of muscle and you burn about 26 kcal more a day: less than half a biscuit.

items.label: Fat
items.note: Nearly idle: about 4.5 kcal per kilogram a day.

items.label: Brain
items.note: 2% of body weight, a fifth of resting energy: neurons are costly to keep ready.

items.label: Liver
items.note: The body's chemical works, busy day and night.

items.label: Heart
items.note: It never rests: 440 kcal per kilogram, and the kidneys match it.
